title: Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine: 20th round of stern EU sanctions hits energy revenues, military-industrial complex, trade and financial services, including crypto
date_evidence: Council of the EU. Press release. 23 April 2026 15:45 (page dateline; meta-SORT_DATE: 20260423)
key_claim: The 20th package lists 46 more shadow-fleet vessels (632 total designated), bans transactions with the ports of Murmansk, Tuapse and Karimun (Indonesia), and creates the basis for a future maritime services ban on Russian crude and products.
frame_summary: The Council frames the 20th package as multi-layered pressure that is progressively closing the shadow fleet's operating space through vessel designations, port bans, tanker-sale due diligence and a maritime-services ban held in reserve.
verbatim_quote: An additional 46 vessels are now subject to a port access ban and a ban on the provision of a broad range of services related to maritime transport, bringing the total number of designated vessels to 632.
verbatim_list: Today’s package includes the basis for a future maritime services ban on Russian crude oil and petroleum products.
Lastly, the package bans transactions with two Russian ports – Murmansk and Tuapse – and with the oil terminal at the port of Karimun in Indonesia, which are used to circumvent the oil price cap.
The 20th package also introduces mandatory due diligence checks for the sale of tankers, thereby making it more difficult for Russia to expand its shadow fleet

title: EU adopts 20th package of sanctions against Russia
date_evidence: News article. 23 April 2026. Directorate-General for Financial Stability, Financial Services and Capital Markets Union (page dateline; also 'Publication date: 23 April 2026' in Details block)
key_claim: Alongside the new listings the EU is pressing flag states to strip shadow-fleet vessels from their registers, while delisting 11 vessels to show a compliance route out of the fleet.
frame_summary: The Commission frames the shadow-fleet measures as an anti-circumvention system: designations plus flag-state outreach plus tanker-sale safeguards and a scrapping clause are meant to shrink the fleet rather than merely tax it.
verbatim_quote: Alongside these additional listings, the EU continues its outreach to flag states to ensure that their registers do not allow these vessels to sail under their flags.
verbatim_list: While 46 vessels are added to the sanctions list, 11 vessels are also delisted in this 20th package, showing that delisting is a possibility for vessels returning to compliance
A new shadow fleet scrapping clause will facilitate the decommissioning or ‘recycling' of vessels and exit from the shadow fleet

title: The shadow fleet is undermining the maritime order more brazenly than ever
key_claim: False-flag Baltic transits nearly quadrupled in the second half of 2025, more than five hundred vessels were reported sailing without valid flag registration, and Russian naval escorts of shadow vessels were formalised in January 2026.
frame_summary: Braw argues the shadow fleet has moved from evasion to open defiance of the maritime order, with stateless sailing, unlisted personnel and naval escorts marking a qualitative erosion of the rules-based shipping system.
verbatim_quote: the number of false-flagged ships in the Baltic Sea quadrupled during the second half of 2025, and in February 2026 the investigative news outlet Follow the Money reported that more than five hundred vessels were sailing without valid flag registration
verbatim_list: In response, Russian military vessels have begun escorting shadow vessels through the English Channel and Baltic Sea.

Such escorts appear to have been formalized in January 2026, when the Russian government’s maritime board decided to take measures that would, from the Russian perspective, protect merchant ships linked to Russia.
notes: In-depth research report by Elisabeth Braw. 91 days old at scan date, at the boundary of the soft 3-month window. Live-fetched 2026-07-22. title: Russian Shadow Fleet Tracker – May 2026: The Russian flag's share of shadow fleet volumes rose to 23%
date_evidence: 8 June 2026 (page dateline under the article title); meta-article:modified_time: 2026-06-08T16:31:28+00:00
key_claim: The Russian flag's share of oil volumes carried by shadow tankers rose from 3% in May 2025 to 23% in April 2026, with at least 30 shadow tankers covered by three Russian insurers and 92% of shadow crude tankers older than 15 years.
frame_summary: KSE Institute documents the shadow fleet consolidating onto Russian state rails, with the Russian flag and Russian insurers replacing squeezed flags of convenience while the fleet ages and its destinations grow more opaque.
verbatim_quote: The share of the Russian flag rose from 3% in May 2025 to 23% of the total volume of oil transported by shadow tankers in April 2026.
verbatim_list: At least 30 shadow tankers operated under coverage from three Russian insurers — AlfaStrakhovanie (17 vessels), Sogaz (10), and Balance Insurance JSC (3).
The top three flag states for shadow tankers were Cameroon, Russia, and Panama, together accounting for 61%.
Among shadow tankers carrying crude oil 92% were over 15 years old, as were the same share of those carrying oil products.

title: Russian Oil Tracker – June 2026: Russia ramps up crude exports after refinery strikes, as a shadow fleet shortage deepens its reliance on Western maritime services
date_evidence: 1 July 2026 (page dateline under the article title)
key_claim: Russian reliance on Western maritime services rose to 42% in May 2026 because the shadow fleet could not carry the additional crude volumes, and six jurisdictions had jointly sanctioned 653 unique oil tankers as of 17 June 2026.
frame_summary: KSE Institute argues the shadow fleet hit a capacity ceiling: refinery strikes forced more crude exports than the parallel fleet could lift, pushing Russia back toward Western tankers and insurance despite the sanctions contest.
verbatim_quote: Russian reliance on Western maritime services increased to 42% in May, IG P&I-insured tankers carried 27% of crude and 73% of oil products.
verbatim_list: but its shadow fleet was insufficient for the additional volume

As of June 17, 2026, the US, UK, EU, Australia, Canada and New Zealand had jointly sanctioned 653 unique oil tankers, including a further 71 and 23 vessels designated in June by the UK and Canada, respectively.
KSE Institute estimates that 185 loaded shadow fleet tankers carrying crude and oil products left Russian ports or were involved in STS transfers in May, 92% of them older than 15 years.

title: Russia's Shadow Fleet Continues to Sail
key_claim: Reflagging to the Russian registry closes the UNCLOS Article 110 stateless/false-flag basis that justified the Deliver and Smyrtos boardings, and Moscow is deliberately encouraging it through draft decrees and SPIEF commitments.
frame_summary: Jamestown (Eurasia Daily Monitor) argues the fleet sits at a critical point: enforcement friction is pushing it under the Russian flag, which trades deniability for legal protection and turns covert evasion into an openly state-associated system.
verbatim_quote: Now that the vessel carries genuine Russian registration, it is neither stateless nor flying a false flag, and thus can no longer be boarded with the same legal justification used in the past.
verbatim_list: The legal justification for seizures such as that of Deliver and Smyrtos lies in Article 110 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), which allows the boarding of a ship that is stateless or suspected of flying a false flag
In June, the Russian Ministry of Transport proposed a draft presidential decree that would make registering ships under the Russian flag quicker and simpler
In May, a draft of a government decree circulated that would allow foreign companies to register in Russia, along with other changes that would make registering under the Russian flag more appealing
Cameroon removed both Smyrtos and Deliver from its ship registry in May, leaving both ships without legitimate documentation and allowing the United Kingdom and France to intervene.

title: Минтранс предложил новую систему регистрации судов под флагом РФ
key_claim: The Russian Transport Ministry's draft presidential decree creates a one-stop registration system under Rosmorrechflot, lets foreign owners carrying Russian cargo apply directly for the Russian flag, and expects up to a thousand ships to move onto the domestic register.
frame_summary: Interfax relays the ministry's framing: simplified registration is merchant-fleet development policy tied to Putin's SPIEF-2026 goal of a top-ten merchant fleet by deadweight, not a sanctions measure.
